parsed.explanation: The combined regime is a hostile national border and custody system layered over a state whose own facility law is comparatively permissive. A trans visitor's home passport meets visa/entry screening that forbids self-declared sex, directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, and can produce lifetime fraud ineligibility; the detention that follows is documented as abusive (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men), and national prisons run conversion-style practices. This state has no restroom ban, its criminalising facility bill died, and a 2019 hate-crime aggravator covers gender identity — but the aggravator has no enforcement record and courts have not relieved the border regime. Minors' gender-affirming care is barred outright, hitting a trans minor traveller. Absence of any criminalisation of trans identity and of documented street-level police sweeps in this state keep it out of the bottom band.

entry_documents.exposure: National order requires binary sex on passports and visas; no self-selection. Cable directs officers to refuse cases where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and to consider a permanent, lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; trans athletes barred from entry; at least eight governments issued advisories after detentions of neighbouring citizens over visas.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-existing X-marked home passports remain valid until expiry; passport litigation pending. No remedy shown operating for visitors at the border.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport meets national visa screening; a marker/presentation mismatch escalates to refusal, additional-evidence demands, or a fraud finding, then to immigration detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented: transgender men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. National corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution) and stopped reporting transgender prisoner counts from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No visitor-facing safeguard, consular or legal-aid route shown working in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at the border feeds directly into immigration detention, where the documented harms occur; prison exposure follows only if criminally charged.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nationally, facility bans cover government buildings in many states; four states criminalise trans restroom use on a trespass trigger, with one documented arrest (handcuffed student, 24 hours in a men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: In this state the law places no restriction on restroom use matching identity; two cities protect it by ordinance; the 2026 facility bill died without a lower-chamber hearing; a 2023 injunction bars school restrictions during litigation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor to this state is safer than the national average, but national travel through ban or criminalisation states re-exposes them; the pending bill could return.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for anyone under 18 (surgery, blockers, hormones) is banned here and was upheld in November 2024, so a trans minor visitor cannot obtain it. National orders denounce such care; hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 records; national insurance rules proposed.
care_services.protection: No protection documented for minors; availability of adult care in this state is not documented.
care_services.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor on hormones faces denial of continuity; adult care status is an open question, not a documented protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'neutralisation' of 'radically pro-transgender' groups; a justice-department reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' (not as a criterion). 2025 polling: 66% back birth-sex markers on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; this state's 2019 law makes gender-identity bias an aggravating circumstance.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing raises institutional suspicion without a documented enforcement lever aimed at individual trans travellers; the state aggravator is paper-only in practice.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors' transition care banned; schools must notify parents in writing if a minor requests a different name or pronoun; a nine-year-old's birth certificate designation was used to restrict her school bathroom; bathroom bill targeted K-12 and universities.
minors_guardians.protection: The 2023 injunction protects one student's school bathroom use during litigation; no protection for visiting minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and, if enrolling the child, compelled disclosure to parents and schools.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data for this state; national bias statistics report only sexual-orientation categories. Polling shows majority discomfort with trans identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime aggravator covering gender identity since 2019; city ordinances protecting restroom use; no data on how police treat trans complainants.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists on paper but no enforcement record; hostility documented is social disapproval (friction), not documented street targeting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport-marker litigation unresolved; the state's 2026 licence-marker ban is under challenge with outcome unrecorded; the facility bill could return; no data on aggravator charging.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, a legal-aid FAQ on document rules, and the school-bathroom injunction; none compels release or entry at the border.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate after the fact and slowly, so they do not neutralise the border, detention or care exposures the record shows recurring.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars trans visitors outright with no remedy; this jurisdiction refuses only on document doubt, but adds documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse in immigration custody plus a lifetime fraud bar — comparable tier, somewhat worse in custody severity, somewhat better in that exclusion is conditional and this state has no facility ban.

Kestrel Isles imposes secondary screening, refused admission and administrative penalties with an appeal desk and no criminal or abusive custody. This jurisdiction sits clearly below: detention is documented as violent and degrading, and refusal can escalate into permanent ineligibility.

Meridia's trained border officers, tribunal appeals, brief detention, release and compensation are the opposite of this record, where custody harm is documented and the border regime is under unresolved challenge. Far above this case.

Varnalia shows organised police targeting — raids, extortion, fines. This state shows no documented street-level police sweeps against trans people, but national custody abuse and the engineered border fraud pathway are more severe, so it sits modestly above that anchor rather than at it.

parsed.synthesis: What a trans visitor meets here is mostly national, not local. Entry screening forbids self-declared sex, directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, and can yield a permanent fraud finding; the detention that follows is documented as abusive, and national prisons run conversion-style practices — state-imposed exposures with no remedy shown working. The state layer is milder than the national average: no restroom ban in force, a criminalising bill that died, city ordinances protecting facility use, and a 2019 gender-identity hate-crime aggravator, though it has no enforcement record. Minors' transition care is banned outright, so a travelling family with a trans minor faces denial. Social disapproval is documented; street-level targeting of trans people in this state is not. The regime is conditional on discovery and detention rather than categorical, which keeps it out of the lowest band.
